newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Indexes busy but not hectic.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Indexes busy but not hectic.

text.p: Trading in U.S. stock index options was busy but not hectic Friday despite a sharp runup in share prices, traders said.
"We're not that busy today, which is strange," said Jay Shartsis, director of options trading at R.F. Lafferty & Co in New York, echoing the sentiment of a couple other options traders.
By about 1415 CDT/1915 GMT, the bellwether Dow industrial average was up 126 points at 7,431. The broader S&P 500 index gained 15 to 858 and June S&P 500 futures were up 14 at 860.
The S&P 100 index added 15 to nearly 838.
"When we're quiet, usually the market goes up," Shartsis said. "So it looks like it's not finished."
But he added that one of his market indicators, the pricing of mirror-image out-of-the-money puts and calls, closed bearish Thursday.
Even so, more such readings would be necessary to suggest strongly that a market top was in place, he said.
"Maybe we're not so far from having a good reaction down," Shartsis said. "Maybe they're just getting all the shorts to cover again.
"But it's tricky in here," he added.

Harrison Roth, a first vice president at Cowen & Co, said the market could be rallying because Treasury bond futures broke through the 111 mark and that bonds could be rallying because of talk of a possible delay in European monetary union.
"That's a pretty slim basis for over 100 points" on the Dow, he said.

Jerry Hegarty, an analyst at Thomson Financial Services said in a report that although the market may be able to hold onto today's gains, it is likely to turn lower by the June expiration in two weeks' time.
Shartsis added that the recent string of heavy call buying -- a bearish contrary indicator -- was broken on Thursday and that put buying was fairly heavy on Friday also.
By 1400 CDT/1900 GMT, OEX put volume was 58,493 compared to call volume of 40,924. SPX put volume was 33,519 versus call volume of 25,671.
The most active OEX puts included the June 820s, the June 800s and the June 830s. Active calls included the June 830s, June 855s and June 860s.
Outside of the June series, the most active OEX options were the July 810 put, the July 825 put and the July 700 puts.
In the SPX, the heaviest turnover was int eh June 800 put, which traded more than 3,800 contracts and the June 880 call, which traded about 3,400.
